text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes often develop slowly over years and include frequent urination, increased thirst, persistent fatigue, and blurred vision.
snippet_highlighted_words: frequent urination, increased thirst, persistent fatigue, and blurred vision

list.snippet: Frequent urination (polyuria): High blood sugar forces your kidneys to work overtime to filter and flush out the excess glucose, which pulls fluids from your tissues and makes you visit the restroom more often, including at night.
Excessive thirst (polydipsia): Because you are losing more fluids through frequent urination, you often feel unusually thirsty and have a dry mouth.
Persistent fatigue: When your cells cannot properly absorb glucose due to insulin resistance, your body lacks its main source of energy.
Blurred vision: Fluctuating blood sugar levels can cause fluid to shift into the lenses of your eyes, temporarily changing their shape and making it hard to focus.
Slow-healing cuts or sores: High blood sugar levels impair circulation and weaken your immune response, making minor wounds take much longer to heal.
Tingling or numbness: Peripheral neuropathy can cause a "pins and needles" sensation, burning, or numbness in your hands, feet, legs, or arms.
Darkened skin patches (acanthosis nigricans): Velvety, dark patches of skin—frequently found in folds like the neck, armpits, or groin—can signal underlying insulin resistance.
Increased hunger or weight changes: You may feel hungrier shortly after eating because energy isn't reaching your cells, or experience unexplained weight changes.
Frequent infections: Higher glucose levels create an environment where yeast and bacteria thrive, leading to recurring urinary tract infections (UTIs) or yeast infections.

text_blocks.snippet: Because many early symptoms are subtle or easy to dismiss, type 2 diabetes is confirmed through simple blood work ordered by a healthcare provider, such as:

list.snippet: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) test (measures average blood sugar over the past 2 to 3 months)
